contributions.statement: Give multi-agent setups one persistent, lookup-only search sub-agent per task that returns file:line pointers instead of pasted excerpts and is told which ranges were edited since its last call; this cut per-episode GPU energy of two existing multi-agent systems by 11-30% at a non-inferior pass rate.
contributions.evidence: §5.2 Tables 4-5, App. G; §3.3 Table 3 attributes excess output to re-exploring overlapping file regions. Audit: single run per configuration, one Qwen3.6 family, Python-only; leave-one-out (Table 8) shows equal or higher pass when removing three of four mechanisms, so the support is for cost, not quality.

contributions.statement: On self-hosted models, cap and shrink output tokens first (pointer-only sub-agent answers, no re-pasted code), because output tokens cost 30-1,000x more GPU energy per token than uncached or cached input tokens.
contributions.evidence: §3.2 Table 2, App. A.2: per-token energy attribution on locally served Qwen3.6 under vLLM. Per-token API billing has a different (smaller) output/input ratio.
relative_to: P24 token/cost budgets (output tokens priced above input)

reason: The Librarian's pointer-only and freshness-report mechanisms are reusable as a host-agnostic subagent definition, and the energy attribution is solid. The paper does not show multi-agent beats single-agent; Table 1's single agent was cheapest.
